summary: This is the core Black Summer NSW declaration, covering roughly 50 council areas across the northern, southern, central and Blue Mountains regions where bushfires burned from spring 2019 into February 2020. Across the whole 2019-20 statewide season, fires burnt around 5.5 million hectares, destroyed about 2,448 homes and killed 25-26 people (figures differ between the coronial inquiry and NSW RFS), including four residents of Bega Valley, three of Eurobodalla, three of Shoalhaven, and firefighters/aircrew killed on duty at Green Valley-Talmalmo and Peak View. Losses also included nearly 400 head of livestock and thousands of kilometres of fencing in single fires such as Adaminaby and Busbys Flat, insured losses in NSW of about $1.88 billion, and hundreds of kilometres of damaged roads; the NSW Government reported paying out more than $1.7 billion in bushfire recovery assistance. Per-fire home-loss counts are compiled separately in data/house_loss/house_loss.csv.

summary: This earlier-starting North Coast declaration covers seven mid-north-coast and northern-rivers council areas where fires ignited from mid-winter 2019 and intensified through spring, well before the broader statewide declaration (AGRN 871) began on 31 August. The Carrai Creek/Carrai East fire complex alone burned nearly 400,000 hectares across Kempsey and Armidale Regional, and the Liberation Trail fire burned around 150,000-175,000 hectares through Clarence Valley. During the worst week of fire weather (7-14 November 2019) the Port Macquarie-Hastings and MidCoast council areas alone lost about 150 homes and one life, despite firefighters saving roughly 3,000 threatened homes; the town of Bobin lost almost two-thirds of its houses. Per-fire home-loss counts (e.g. Busbys Flat, Liberation Trail, Kian Road) are compiled separately in data/house_loss/house_loss.csv.

declaration_name: Tamworth (Halls Creek Road) Bushfire: 3 January 2019 onwards
summary: A single bushfire on Halls Creek Road threatened rural properties on the outskirts of Tamworth in early January 2019, burning around 600 hectares of bushland in windy conditions. Local news coverage reported that although multiple small and large rural properties on Kalinda Road were under threat, RFS crews and bulldozer containment lines protected the area and no homes were reported destroyed. No official casualty, livestock or dollar-loss figures were found for this declaration; it appears to have been a comparatively minor, single-LGA event.

declaration_name: Parkes and Cabonne (Curembenya) Bushfire: 5 January 2019 onwards
summary: The Curembenya fire burned over roughly 4,500 hectares across the Parkes and Cabonne council areas in early January 2019, threatening a number of rural properties. According to the Australian Government's own disaster-assistance media release, no properties were destroyed, which officials credited to community preparedness and the firefighting response; no deaths, injuries or other loss figures were located.

main_fires: Ash Island / Kooragang Island Waste Emplacement Facility fire
summary: A roughly 100-hectare vegetation fire broke out on Ash Island in the Hunter River estuary on 5 January 2019 and was contained relatively quickly by Fire and Rescue NSW and RFS crews. Its main ongoing significance was that it is believed to have smouldered underground afterwards into a long-running subsurface fire at the former BHP steelworks waste landfill (discovered burning on 28 January 2019), which became a separate environmental and public-works remediation issue rather than a conventional bushfire-loss event. No homes, deaths or agricultural losses were reported for the original bushfire.

This declaration covers bushfire activity in the Snowy Valleys LGA (around Adelong/Tumut) from 17 January 2019, roughly a year before the same area was devastated by the far larger Dunns Road fire of the 2019-20 Black Summer season. No news coverage or official impact figures specific to the January 2019 event were located; searches instead returned material about the unrelated, much larger December 2019-January 2020 Dunns Road fire in the same LGA (which destroyed around 180-193 homes and is already captured in the house_loss.csv per-fire dataset under AGRN 871). This January 2019 declaration appears to have been a comparatively minor, contained event.
